headline: Sensex plunges near 1,000 points driven by crude oil spike and IT stock selloff

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Crude oil prices spiked near $116 per barrel, putting pressure on Indian equity markets.
IT sector heavyweights faced sharp sell-offs, with the Nifty IT index falling over 3%.
Market participants remained cautious ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's interest rate decision.
Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) outflows continued to weigh heavily on market sentiment.
whatHappening: Sensex cracked up to 995 points while Nifty traded near the 22,500 mark.
L&T shares surged 6% following a 33% year-on-year increase in Q2 net profit.
HUL posted a 4% rise in Q2 net profit to ₹2,790 crore with a 7% volume growth.
Jio Platforms received 'Buy' ratings from Nomura, Motilal, and Elara on Day 1 of coverage.
summary: Indian benchmark indices plunged sharply on October 28 as rising crude oil prices and IT stock sell-offs spooked investors. Persistent FPI outflows and caution ahead of the U.S. Fed decision further dampened sentiment. However, stock-specific gains were witnessed in L&T and HUL following strong Q2 financial results.
